answer: Decaying memory-collateral rent. Each identity must post a memory reserve whose required size grows with the number of sibling identities created from the same device or network fingerprint. A quill of registration data is hashed into a per-cluster salt; the reserve scales as the square of sibling count, so the tenth clone pays roughly a hundredfold the tenth's marginal reserve. An ember of the reserve is returned only after sustained independent activity. A prism check samples and recomputes the salt to catch forged fingerprints.
